predictions.title: Hot days in Mar–Apr 2027
predictions.method: Year-to-year spread of bias-adjusted POWER Tmax 2001–2025 (median, 10th–90th percentile), shifted by the CMIP6 SSP2-4.5 2030s median change.

predictions.title: Aman 2026 crop condition
predictions.method: Peak MODIS NDVI Sep–Nov this year, against the 2001–2025 peaks (20th–80th percentile shown).

predictions.title: Best Boro transplant window 2026–27
predictions.method: Expected heat (≥35 °C) and cold (<15 °C) days during flowering, ~70 days after transplanting, from POWER 2011–2025.

crops.name: Boro rice
crops.source: FAO-56 Table 12; BRRI Adhunik Dhaner Chash

crops.name: Boro rice (AWD)
crops.source: FAO-56; IRRI/BRRI alternate wetting and drying

rotations.name: Boro – Fallow – T. Aman
rotations.note: What most farmers around Ashulia grow. Boro needs a lot of pumped water, and the land sits empty in June and December.

rotations.name: Boro (AWD) – Fallow – T. Aman
rotations.note: Same crops, but let the Boro field dry out for a few days between waterings (AWD). Saves about a quarter of the water.

rotations.name: Mustard – Late Boro – T. Aman
rotations.note: Adds a quick mustard crop before a later Boro. More income, but the Boro then flowers in hot April.

rotations.name: Mustard – Mungbean – T. Aman
rotations.note: Grows mustard and mungbean instead of Boro. Far less pumping, and mungbean feeds the soil for the next crop.

rotations.name: Maize – Mungbean – T. Aman
rotations.note: Winter maize instead of Boro: sells well and needs half the water. Mungbean after it feeds the soil.
